comparator.sourceNotes: Current adopted OER Articles 3–10 establishes the ordinary programme and 165 unique displayed EC after counting each repeated module once. questionsApplications.label: How do literary and media forms express and interpret culture?
How do language and the brain interact?
How do European institutions and histories shape Dutch–German cultural relations?

alternatives.concept: A programme studying literary form, language and meaning through close reading, stylistics, psycholinguistics, film/media interpretation and humanities research. Historical, social-theoretical, European political and philosophical courses supply specific cultural contexts; this is broader study rather than German-specialist formation.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Literary Studies Practical literary interpretation, narrative form, close reading and critical sources directly implement the literary-analysis discipline; no German corpus is implied.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation”.

basisLabels: Academic expression, rhetoric and intercultural communication
courseTraceability.rationale: The Art of Rhetorical Communication Rhetorical theory, argument and persuasive speaking support analysis and practice of academic/public expression; it does not teach German proficiency.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Academic expression, rhetoric and intercultural communication”.

basisLabels: German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context
courseTraceability.rationale: Modern History Modern nationalism, ideologies, industrialisation and world wars provide specific historical context for interpreting modern German/European cultural questions, without a German-specialist sequence.. It implements the explicit academic basis “German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context”.

basisLabels: Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition
Language processing and cognition
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Brain & Behavior Brain anatomy, neural signalling and psychological processes provide the necessary taught foundation for Psycholinguistics; not a substitute for German grammar.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition” and “Language processing and cognition”.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition
courseTraceability.rationale: Style & Meaning Grammar, discourse, cognition, narration and text worlds connect linguistic choices to literary interpretation through actual stylistic analysis.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation” and “Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition”.

basisLabels: Academic expression, rhetoric and intercultural communication
courseTraceability.rationale: Rhetoric in Action Actual public speaking, debate, storytelling and primary-school rhetorical activities develop communication and reflective teaching practice, without German subject-teaching equivalence.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Academic expression, rhetoric and intercultural communication”.

basisLabels: Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition
Language processing and cognition
courseTraceability.rationale: Psycholinguistics Actual language acquisition, bilingualism, comprehension/production and experimental language inquiry supply a direct language-and-brain contribution.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition” and “Language processing and cognition”.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
courseTraceability.rationale: World Myth & Literature Comparative myth, narrative transmission and literary theory provide a comparative literary contribution, not German myth/corpus teaching.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation”.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Film & Media Film form, expressionism, adaptation and independent interpretation provide concrete film/media analytical methods; not a complete German film-history sequence.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation”.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context
courseTraceability.rationale: Media Archaeology Print, optical and sound media as cultural artifacts supply material-historical methods for studying mediated culture, not specifically German media content.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation” and “German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context”.

basisLabels: German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context
Humanities research and philosophical/cultural reflection
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Sociology Classical theories including Marx and Weber, modernity and stratification supply specific social-theoretical tools for interpreting culture and historical change.. It implements the explicit academic basis “German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context” and “Humanities research and philosophical/cultural reflection”.

basisLabels: Humanities research and philosophical/cultural reflection
courseTraceability.rationale: Qualitative Research Methodology Interviews, textual/documentary and visual analysis, coding, reflexivity and research ethics provide concrete empirical humanities/cultural-research complements.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Humanities research and philosophical/cultural reflection”.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
courseTraceability.rationale: Life & Travel Writing Life narratives, memory, identity and cultural positioning are analysed through close reading and comparative research; it is not a German study-abroad replacement.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation”.

basisLabels: Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation

basisLabels: German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context
courseTraceability.rationale: European Union Politics Actual European institutions, integration and policy-document inquiry provide a specific institutional complement to the evidenced Netherlands/Germany/Europe questions; it is not German political-history teaching.. It implements the explicit academic basis “German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context”.

basisLabels: German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context

It implements the explicit academic basis “German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context” and “Humanities research and philosophical/cultural reflection”.

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation

basisLabels: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation

notes.text: The UCR programme offers broader literary, language and cultural analysis. It does not provide advanced German proficiency, a German-language literary-history and linguistics sequence, German subject-teaching preparation or the required German-speaking-country experience.

audience.programmeDescription: German Language and Culture studies German language, literature, linguistics and cultural life, including Dutch–German relations and European contexts. It combines advanced German proficiency, academic inquiry and a required period of study in a German-speaking country.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A broader UCR programme in literary interpretation, language analysis and cultural inquiry meaningfully addresses the confirmed scholarly core, without reproducing German-specialist formation or the unknown later requirements. The unknown required 15 EC are not compared. UCR does not supply advanced German proficiency, the German literary/linguistic sequence, German subject-teaching preparation or the required overseas language experience.

curriculum.limitation: The current regulations repeat three 5-EC modules. The displayed 165 distinct EC are a supported subset of a nominal 180-EC degree; 15 EC of required later study and its replacement/rotation allocation remain unresolved.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic-core comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The independently confirmed literary, language, cultural and research study, together with its separate 30-EC open semester and 30-EC restricted Arts minor space: 165 distinct documented EC.
comparisonScope.excluded: The unidentified 15 EC of required later replacement/rotation study, any dependent advanced or pedagogical culmination, and certification of a complete ordinary external pathway.

componentNotes.y2-abroad: Required 15-EC study period in a German-speaking country.
componentNotes.y2-minors: 30 EC of bachelor-level courses to broaden your studies, excluding courses from your own programme. Study abroad requires advance approval.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: 10-EC bachelor research project and tutorial. Entry requires the first humanities research-methods course.
componentNotes.y3-minors: 30 EC normally filled with two Faculty of Arts minors. A separate route applies under the stated educational-minor or mobility conditions.

acceptance.claim: A broader UCR programme in literary interpretation, language analysis and cultural inquiry meaningfully addresses the confirmed scholarly core, without reproducing German-specialist formation or the unknown later requirements.
acceptance.targetContext: Exact Radboud German Language and Culture ordinary 2026–2027 programme. No Article 6 exception, old curriculum or future prospective-year table is imported.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified source-first second pass by the same AI against actual official source and UCR content and exact finished inputs; not independent human/separate-agent review.

uncertainties.fact: The current regulations repeat three 5-EC modules. The displayed 165 distinct EC are a supported subset of a nominal 180-EC degree; 15 EC of required later study and its replacement/rotation allocation remain unresolved.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The missing later 15 EC are advanced German literary/cultural courses.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Full German-specialist training would be stronger/different, but the confirmed literary/language core and broader UCR analytical response remain. No unknown later component is aligned.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The missing later 15 EC emphasise advanced linguistics or German-as-foreign-language pedagogy, or require an applicable rotation/replacement combination.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: This could materially change full final-year training and the closest specialist emphasis. The deliberately limited confirmed-core claim survives; German proficiency/didactics and unknown later study are not supplied or certified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: An applicable rule permits distinct thematic offerings under the repeated module codes.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: The additional thematic content and credit permission would change the full external allocation; it is not assumed. The independently confirmed core and broader UCR analytical response remain, while those extra offerings stay outside this comparison.
